question: Net new assets by quarter for each of the five, with each firm's own definition of the metric.

claims.text: Quarterly net new assets - Morgan Stanley (Wealth Management segment, calendar quarters): On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025) the CFO said net new assets for the quarter were $94 billion, a 6% annualized growth rate of beginning period assets.
Quarterly net new assets - Morgan Stanley: the Wealth Management financial supplement (published 2026-07-15) shows net new assets of $59.2 billion for the quarter ended Jun 30, 2025.
Quarterly net new assets - Morgan Stanley: the Wealth Management supplement (published 2026-10-14) shows $81.0 billion for the quarter ended Sep 30, 2025.

Quarterly net new assets - Morgan Stanley: the 4Q25 supplement (published 2026-01-15) shows $122.3 billion for the quarter ended Dec 31, 2025; the 4Q25 press release shows $356.3 billion for full-year 2025.

Quarterly net new assets - Morgan Stanley: the 1Q26 10-Q (published 2026-05-05) says Wealth Management added net new assets of $118 billion; the supplement published 2026-07-15 gives $118.4 billion for the quarter ended Mar 31, 2026.

Quarterly net new assets - Morgan Stanley: for 2Q26 (press release 2026-07-15; supplement) net new assets were $148.1 billion; the firm said just over half represented inflows related to IPOs of certain clients in its Workplace channel.

Quarterly net new assets - Morgan Stanley: for 3Q26 (press release 2026-10-14) the firm reported record net new assets of $232 billion ($232.4 billion in the supplement), with just over half associated with IPO-related flows. On the 3Q26 call the CFO said IPO-related flows contributed just over half of NNA and that flows will fluctuate as lockups expire, funds make distributions and individuals use assets for consumption.

Quarterly net new assets - Schwab (reported as core net new assets): the 3Q25 10-Q (November 2025) states core net new assets of $137.5 billion in the third quarter of 2025 and $355.5 billion in the first nine months.
Quarterly net new assets - Schwab: the 4Q25 press release (2026-01-21) reports record 4Q core net new assets of $163.9 billion, bringing 2025 asset gathering to $519.4 billion.

Quarterly net new assets - Schwab: on the 1Q26 call (April 2026) the CEO said that, excluding a onetime mutual fund clearing outflow, Schwab attracted $158 billion in core net new assets, a first quarter record.

Quarterly net new assets - Schwab: the 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) states core net new assets of $119.8 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up 49% from 2Q25, and $259.8 billion for the first half of 2026.

Quarterly net new assets - Schwab: the 3Q26 press release (2026-10-15) quotes the CEO that Schwab was entrusted with $190.4 billion in core net new assets in the third quarter, an annualized growth rate of 5.8%.

Quarterly net new assets - Edward Jones: the 2Q25 10-Q (published 2025-08-08) shows net new assets of $17 billion for the second quarter of 2025 (-10% versus 2Q24). The 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) shows $17 billion for the third quarter of 2025 (+6%) and $51 billion for the nine months.
Quarterly net new assets - Edward Jones: the 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) shows net new assets of $74 billion for the full year 2025, which management called relatively flat compared to 2024.

Quarterly net new assets - Edward Jones: the 1Q26 10-Q (published 2026-05-07) shows $18 billion for the first quarter of 2026 versus $17 billion a year earlier (+4%); the 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) shows $18 billion for the second quarter versus $17 billion (+6%), and $36 billion for the first half versus $34 billion.

Quarterly net new assets - Raymond James (reported as Domestic Private Client Group net new assets, fiscal quarters ending in the month shown): the supplement published 2025-10-22 shows $14,020 million for the quarter ended December 2024 (4.0% annualized growth) and $8,830 million for March 2025 (2.6%).

Quarterly net new assets - Raymond James: the supplement published 2026-07-22 shows Domestic PCG net new assets of $11,651 million (June 2025 quarter, 3.4% annualized), $17,930 million (September 2025, 5.0%), $30,828 million (December 2025, 8.0%), $22,954 million (March 2026, 5.8%) and $21,692 million (June 2026, 5.5%), with $75,474 million for the nine months ended June 2026.

Quarterly net new assets - Raymond James: the fiscal third quarter 2026 press release (2026-07-22) reports Domestic Private Client Group net new assets of $21.7 billion, or annualized growth from beginning-of-quarter assets of 5.5%.

Definition of net new assets - Morgan Stanley: the 3Q26 supplement (published 2026-10-14) and press release say net new assets represent client asset inflows, including interest, dividends and asset acquisitions, less client asset outflows, and exclude the impact of business combinations/divestitures and the impact of fees and commissions. The 2025 10-K uses the same wording and adds that NNA is influenced by factors such as macro conditions, seasonality, advisor and client retention and large idiosyncratic inflows and outflows including single large client events.

Definition of net new assets - Schwab: Schwab's headline metric is core net new assets. A note in the 3Q26 deck (2026-10-15) defines it as net new assets before significant one-time flows, such as acquisitions/divestitures or extraordinary flows (generally greater than $25 billion; $10 billion in prior periods) relating to a specific client, and activity from off-platform Schwab Bank Retail CDs; these flows may span multiple reporting periods.

Definition of net new assets - Schwab: Schwab's 2Q26 press release (2026-07-21) notes that, unless otherwise noted, differences between net new assets and core net new assets are net flows from off-platform Schwab Bank Retail CDs. The 2025 10-K glossary (published 2026-02-25) defines 'net new client assets' as total inflows of client cash and securities to Schwab less client outflows, where inflows include dividends and interest, outflows include commissions and fees, and capital gains distributions are excluded.

Definition of net new assets - Edward Jones: the 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states that net new assets represents cash and securities inflows and outflows, excluding mutual fund capital gain distributions received by U.S. clients.

Definition of net new assets - Edward Jones: the 2026 10-Qs (1Q26 published 2026-05-07; 2Q26 published 2026-08-07) state that net new assets represents cash and securities inflows and outflows, including fees and commissions and excluding mutual fund capital gain distributions received by U.S. clients.

Definition of net new assets - Raymond James: its supplement (published 2026-07-22) and press release say Domestic Private Client Group net new assets represents domestic PCG client inflows, including dividends and interest, less domestic PCG client outflows, including commissions, advisory fees and other fees. The annualized growth percentage is based on the beginning domestic PCG assets under administration balance for the period. The measure covers the domestic PCG only.

Closest flow measure - Morgan Stanley: besides net new assets, Morgan Stanley reports fee-based asset flows, which its press release (2026-10-14) says include net new fee-based assets (including asset acquisitions), net account transfers, dividends, interest and client fees, and exclude institutional cash management related activity.

Closest flow measure - Morgan Stanley: fee-based asset flows were $45.6 billion in the quarter ended Dec 31, 2025 (supplement published 2026-01-15), $53.7 billion in the quarter ended Mar 31, 2026 (supplement published 2026-07-15), and $41.9 billion (Sep 30, 2025), $39.1 billion (Jun 30, 2026) and $80.5 billion (Sep 30, 2026) in the supplement published 2026-10-14.

Closest flow measure - Edward Jones: besides net new assets, its 10-Q (2025 Q3, published 2025-11-07) defines 'client dollars invested' for advisory programs revenue as the net of the inflows and outflows of client dollars into advisory programs (for trade revenue, the principal amount of clients' buy and sell transactions resulting in revenue).

Closest flow measure - Raymond James: the firm reports net new assets under the name 'Domestic Private Client Group net new assets' (see p1 and p2). Its 3Q fiscal 2026 press release (2026-07-22) separately attributes asset management fee growth partly to net inflows into PCG fee-based accounts, without a dollar figure for those inflows.

adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's. The household count is a client-count measure, not a dollar flow.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says the net client AUM flows represent the net change in clients' AUM balances over a specified period, excluding market appreciation/depreciation and other adjustments.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's. This defines AUM flows, not a net new assets metric.
